fields.v: Watanabe, K., Ogawa, H., Ito, S., Nakazawa, T., Tsuru, K. (2026). A Knowledge Engineering Framework for AI-Driven Software Development: Harness, Guardrail, and AI-Native Knowledge DevOps. In 2026 17th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA), IEEE. doi:10.1109/IISA71656.2026.11705457
Conference (IISA 2026, IEEE; 4-page short paper)
Digital Innovation R&D, Hitachi, Ltd., Japan (all five authors)

Proposes an approach (knowledge engineering framework: Effective Agent = Foundation Model + (Harness || Guardrail), plus AI-Native Knowledge DevOps meta-process); secondary: evaluates it descriptively in a 142-day single-developer experience report (N=1)
Harness / Guardrail / AI-Native Knowledge DevOps framework (authors' own); no version. Builds on ADRs, GitOps, AGENTS.md/harness-engineering corpora 'as foundations rather than novelty'

Harness: Knowledge artifacts (CLAUDE.md rules, DESIGN_NOTES.md design notes in ADR form: context, alternatives, rationale, consequences), Skills (SKILL.md parameterised procedures: commit, deployment, review, issue lifecycle), Stakeholder persona sub-agent prompts (business, end-user, UX, architect, implementer, tester, QA, operations, adversarial critic), Runtime/loader. Guardrail: lint, unit/E2E/visual regression tests, adversarial review-gate on a different model family, post-push review Skill. All versioned in one Git repository with CI/CD definitions (GitOps)

Operational: Harness (pre-action course-setting) -> agent action -> Guardrail (pre-merge gates: deterministic checks + cross-family review-gate; post-merge post-push review). Meta-process AI-Native Knowledge DevOps across sessions: Capture findings -> Refine artifacts -> Create artifacts (when novel) -> Apply artifacts back into Harness and Guardrail (Fig. 1). CI/CD: push -> lint -> test+VRT -> build -> staging (automatic) -> production (manual) (Fig. 2)

Refine/Create/Apply proposals traverse the same pull-request/CI gates as code ('human-governed, agent-assisted'); manual approval for production deployment; review-gate critiques must be rebutted or addressed before merge (by whom not fully stated)
Full workflow (framework applied over the whole 142-day project); cross-family review-gate effect explicitly 'untested'; full agent execution of Knowledge DevOps 'not demonstrated'
Not classifiable (knowledge/context-artifact framework; no specification as the main artefact); authors do not use SDD terms
New project (production-grade market-sizing web application built over 142 days)

Single project: 9,441 application SLOC / 8,773 test SLOC; 297 commits over 142 days; 441 tests (278 unit / 156 E2E / 7 VRT); 14 knowledge documents (7,349 lines); 42 CLAUDE.md rules, 56 design notes; 92 issues (78 via the agent's issue-lifecycle Skill)

Business planning: TAM/SAM/SOM market-sizing web wizard using a cloud-hosted reasoning LLM with web search; three deployment tiers including closed-network production for confidential business plans. Programming language Not stated
Single developer, overlapping with the framework authors

Criterion: none formal (descriptive experience report; 'we make no causal claim'). - Framework + Claude Code (implementation agent) + OpenAI Codex CLI review-gate (openai-codex plugin); models and versions Not stated: 297 commits, 9,441 SLOC, 441 tests, zero main CI/CD failures after setup, 63% maintenance-class commits on agent-loaded artifacts, URL hallucination not recurring after rule. Quality verdict: partly (descriptive only, no baseline). Cost verdict: not measured
No comparison: single case, no baseline ('We did not record per-critique counts or a same-family baseline'). Repetitions: 1. Human intervention: PR/CI gates, manual production approval

N=1, single developer (overlapping with authors), single platform (Claude Code), single domain; individual-skill, post-hoc, survivorship, Hawthorne risks; maintenance-class single-rater regex; line counts descriptive proxies; commit increase not isolatable from ramp-up/scope/deadline; living documentation not separable from author skill.
